questions.question: A stone is projected vertically upwards with a velocity of 49 m/s. Taking $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$, find the time taken to reach maximum height, the maximum height and the total time of flight. Ignore air resistance.
questions.solution:
**Given:** $u = 49\ \text{m/s},\ g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$ (upward positive, so $a = -9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$)

**Step 1 — Time to reach maximum height:**
At maximum height the vertical velocity becomes zero, $v = 0$.
$$v = u + at \;\Rightarrow\; 0 = 49 - 9.8t$$
$$\boxed{t = 5\ \text{s}}$$

**Step 2 — Maximum height:**
$$h = u t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 49 \times 5 - \frac{1}{2}(9.8)(25) = 245 - 122.5$$
$$\boxed{h = 122.5\ \text{m}}$$
(Equivalently $h = u^2/2g = 2401/19.6 = 122.5\ \text{m}$ ✓)

**Step 3 — Total time of flight** (time up equals time down by symmetry):
$$\boxed{T = 2t = 10\ \text{s}}$$
questions.knowledgeNote: For vertical projection, time to reach the top is u over g, max height is u squared over 2g, and flight time is twice that.
